title: Startup healthcheck interval ignored when startup command is omitted
body:
### Issue Description

[The Podman 6.2.0 release notes](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/releases/tag/v6.2.0) state:

> When a startup healthcheck interval is specified, but no startup healthcheck command, the standard healthcheck command will be used instead

However, when `--health-cmd` and `--health-startup-interval` are provided without `--health-startup-cmd`, the healthcheck seems to follow the regular healthcheck interval and the startup interval is not used.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Create a container with an explicit startup healthcheck command and a one-second startup interval. After five seconds, the healthcheck has run multiple times:

    ```bash
    podman run --rm -d --name explicit --health-cmd false --health-startup-interval 1s --health-startup-cmd false alpine sleep 30
    sleep 5
    podman inspect explicit --format '{{len .State.Health.Log}}'
    ```

2. Create a container with the same healthcheck and startup interval, but omit the startup healthcheck command. After five seconds, the healthcheck has run only once:

    ```bash
    podman run --rm -d --name fallback --health-cmd false --health-startup-interval 1s alpine sleep 30
    sleep 5
    podman inspect fallback --format '{{len .State.Health.Log}}'
    ```

### Describe the results you received

The container with an explicit startup healthcheck command records multiple healthcheck executions.

The container without an explicit startup healthcheck command records only one execution. It does not continue running the healthcheck at the specified one-second startup interval.

### Describe the results you expected

Both containers should run the healthcheck at approximately one-second intervals during startup.

According to the Podman 6.2.0 release notes, when a startup healthcheck interval is specified without a startup healthcheck command, Podman should use the standard healthcheck command instead.
